clue.text: The rough stuff put ministers under fire

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed under another comes after it

parts.note: to fire someone is to sack them
the cloth is a collective term for the clergy

explanation.surface: Ministers face a rough time after being thrown out of office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts the clergy word below the dismissal word in this down entry; 'put' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sackcloth is a coarse fabric woven from flax or hemp, rough material worn in penance.

clue.text: Step outside the hotel to see a boat

indicators.note: the stepping word goes around the outside of the lodging word

parts.note: a pace is a single step
an inn is a small hotel

explanation.surface: Someone walks out of a hotel to look at a boat in the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnace is a small ship's boat, rowed or sailed, carried aboard a larger vessel.

clue.text: Country-loving

parts.note: a person who loves their country and is devoted to its welfare

explanation.definitionFit: Patriotism is devotion to one's nation, so the adjective describes a lover of the homeland.

clue.text: An advocate of substance retained by a great explorer

indicators.note: the explorer holds on to the substance, so it is attached to his name as his

parts.note: Marco Polo, the Venetian traveller to China
the gist of something is its substance or essence

explanation.surface: A supporter of real substance is kept on by a famous explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: The explorer is Marco Polo; 'retained by' attaches the substance word after his name, and 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologist is someone who argues in defence of a cause or belief, its champion.

clue.text: Whispered comments when cut by the party

indicators.note: the word for when is split open by the word for party

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a side is a party in a dispute or contest

explanation.surface: Remarks muttered when a political party slices into the debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Asides are remarks made quietly to one listener, or to the audience, not meant for all.

clue.text: A knight would use a spear a great deal

parts.note: a lance is a long cavalry spear
a lot means a great deal

explanation.surface: A mounted warrior would make heavy use of a spear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would use' and the 'a' before 'spear' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancelot is the most famous knight of King Arthur's Round Table.

clue.text: Greek maid serving girl with a non-alcoholic drink

parts.note: gal is an informal word for girl
tea is a drink with no alcohol

explanation.surface: A Greek maid serves a girl a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Galatea is the statue Pygmalion carved, brought to life as a maiden.

clue.text: Isle (Man) maybe seen as having great potential

indicators.note: 'maybe' says the letters given might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: The Isle of Man might be regarded as full of promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' signals rearranging ISLE and MAN together; 'seen as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Seminal work is formative and influential, containing the seeds of later development.

clue.text: Oddly enough, men fail to get excited

indicators.note: something done oddly is done in a strange way, so these letters come out in a strange order

explanation.surface: Curiously, men don't manage to become worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly enough' shuffles MEN and FAIL; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflame, used intransitively, is to become heated or roused with passion.

clue.text: The sort followed by blushing relatives

indicators.note: the colour word comes after the type word

parts.note: a kind is a sort or type
someone blushing goes red

explanation.surface: A type of person is pursued by embarrassed family members.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred are one's family members, people related by blood.

clue.text: Woman making a home Ireland — English

indicators.note: the dwelling word makes its place within the poetic Irish name

parts.note: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland
a nest is a home

explanation.surface: A woman sets up house in Ireland, though she is English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a' has the home word set up inside the old name for Ireland, ERIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernestine is a female first name, so it identifies a particular woman.

clue.text: Soldiers go ahead of reporters to check

indicators.note: the soldiers come before the reporters in the entry

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
the press is the body of journalists

explanation.surface: Troops march ahead of the journalists to keep them in check.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress is to restrain or hold back, as when keeping an urge in check.

clue.text: The French set about bridge game

indicators.note: the French article is placed around the spanning word

parts.note: le is French for the
to bridge something is to stretch across it

explanation.surface: French players start a game of bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' looks like the card game but means spanning; 'set about' puts LE around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a field game played with netted sticks, originally from North America.

clue.text: A fortune-teller makes nothing awfully clear

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the letters are mangled

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant makes absolutely nothing plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges CLEAR to RACLE; 'makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is a prophet or seer whose pronouncements foretell what is to come.

clue.text: Scan written notes

parts.note: to scan a text is to read it
music in printed form is notation, written notes

explanation.surface: A musician looks over a score.
explanation.definitionFit: Running one's eye over a score and understanding its notation is the skill of sight-reading notation.

clue.text: Rapture shown about set end-rate plant

indicators.note: the happiness word is shown around the grade letter

parts.note: euphoria is rapture, intense happiness
B is the second grade, so second-rate

explanation.surface: Delight is shown at a mediocre plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'set end-rate' is an OCR slip for 'second-rate', B as a grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphorbia is a genus of spurges, plants with milky sap such as the poinsettia.

clue.text: To repeat it with little hesitation satisfied a natural urge

parts.note: er is a small hesitant sound
someone who ate satisfied hunger

explanation.surface: Saying it again with a brief pause, someone satisfies an appetite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; the natural urge is hunger.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to say or do something again, time after time.

clue.text: Spare ruler, it's thought

parts.note: spare can mean lean or thin
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A monarch with time to spare, so it is believed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare' looks like extra but means lean; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinking as a noun is thought, the mental activity of considering ideas.

clue.text: Intuitive feeling about a joint

indicators.note: the feeling word is wrapped about the letter a

parts.note: a hunch is an intuitive feeling

explanation.surface: Someone has a gut feeling regarding a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a hip or knee, which is fair, but here it is a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A haunch is a leg and loin of meat, a butcher's joint, or the hip of a person.

clue.text: Reach an arrangement for the weaver

indicators.note: reaching an arrangement suggests putting these letters in a new order

explanation.surface: Coming to an agreement on behalf of the weaver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges REACH and AN; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Arachne was a mortal weaver turned into a spider by Athena.

clue.text: Striking due to a shortage of food

parts.note: no means none, a complete shortage
a table can mean the food served, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: Workers walk out because there is not enough to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' suggests industrial action but means remarkable; 'due to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Notable means remarkable, worthy of attention, just as something striking catches the eye.

clue.text: Royal family rolls embellished with gold

parts.note: to wind a thread is to roll it up
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: The monarchy's bread rolls are decorated with gold leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embellished with' is a link; OR is gold in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: Windsor has been the name of the British royal house since 1917.

clue.text: Port and a snack

definitions.meaning: a town on the Kent coast, one of England's historic Cinque Ports
two slices of bread with a filling between them

explanation.definitionFit: Sandwich is a Kent port town, and the snack is named after the Earl who took his title from it.

clue.text: The ratification of a certain point caused much pleasure

parts.note: a specific compass point, south, abbreviated S
music that sent you delighted you

explanation.surface: Approval of a particular matter delighted everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; 'sent' in this sense means thrilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Assent is formal agreement, as royal assent ratifies a bill into law.

clue.text: Test a tin's contents for poor quality

indicators.note: the contents of a tin get jumbled up, so its letters are mixed

explanation.surface: An inspector checks what is inside a tin for shoddiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents' rearranges TEST A TINS; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattiness is shabbiness, a worn and cheap condition.

clue.text: A plumber and fitter

definitions.meaning: one who plumbs, measuring the depth of water with a line

explanation.definitionFit: A sounder measures depth as a plumb line does, and sounder means in better health.

clue.text: Such a blissful meal must include wine

indicators.note: the phrase must include the answer, held within its letters

explanation.surface: A delightful dinner ought to come with some wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must include' signals the answer running through 'Such a blissful'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chablis is a dry white Burgundy, named after its town.

clue.text: A capital Biro in a faulty condition

indicators.note: a pen in faulty condition is broken, so its letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A capital-letter pen that isn't working properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty condition' rearranges BIRO IN A; a Biro is a British ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya.

clue.text: Put off a fellow cleaner

parts.note: to deter is to put off
a gent is a fellow, a man

explanation.surface: Discourage a man from being the cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a cleansing agent used for washing.
